text:
alex kim: Heads-up — planning to roll out a config change for routing + quota smoothing to avoid cold-surge on model variants. Thinking staggered cohort fanout + per-cohort quota smoothing. Dry-run tomorrow 08:00 UTC. Thoughts?

maria gonzalez: sounds good. what are cohort sizes? how do we pick them for multimodel traffic?

alex kim: proposal: 6 cohorts exponential: 0.1%, 0.5%, 2%, 5%, 20%, 72% — ramp every 15m with hotspot detection. Quotas: smoothing window 5m token-rate + max-burst 2x. runtime flags: `cohort_fanout` + `quota_smoothing_ms`.

jon rao: can we attach telemetry hooks per cohort? need per-model token & error metrics. if latency > SLO we should auto-stop next ramp.

tara li: yeah add `telemetry.cohort` tag, and a bridge event for console — want per-cohort dashboard tiles. also need a kill switch in console (one-click pause).

kevin ng: impl detail — runtime prefix caching can skew quota signals. cohorts hitting cached prefixes show low token burn. suggest also measure requests/sec + unique-kv-hits to detect cache skew.

alex kim: good point. include `cache_hit_ratio` vs baseline and fallback to sampling cold requests for health signal.

deploy-bot: scheduled job created: `config-dryrun-staggered-fanout` -> staging at 1765558000 (canary).

maria gonzalez: :thumbsup: i'll draft console mockups for per-cohort tiles. quick UX q: show cumulative percentage or per-cohort? i'd vote cumulative for rollout clarity.

jon rao: both — per-cohort + cumulative. ops will want ability to mute cohorts.

tara li: +1. also require audit log entry for each cohort activation with commit id + operator.

alex kim: will update the RFC and open PR for runtime flags: `cohort_fanout_schedule`, `quota_smoothing_window_ms`, `cohort_telemetry_tags`. PR: https://git.redwood/team/runtime/pull/432

kevin ng: preflight checklist suggestion: 1) perf test w/ synthetic 50 qps 2) console tile integration 3) rollback playbook 4) notify customer-success + support

alex kim: adding checklist items. i'll ping #customer-success when dry-run starts. thanks y'all.
